errorCodes.meaning: The supplied cursor is unrecognised, expired, or was minted for a different set of filters. A producer restarts the enumeration.

`listId` names no list in this context. Distinct from an empty page on purpose: a list is the holder's own, and "no such list" is a definite answer a client should act on (it was deleted elsewhere) rather than render as an empty list.

DirectoryEntryId.description: A community directory entry's identifier, exactly as that community's directory returned it. Opaque and community-scoped: the agent stores and compares it as a string, never parses it, and never treats the same value under two communities as the same entry.
DirectoryEntryId.title: DirectoryEntryId

DirectoryRef.description: Links a contact to the entry in a community's member directory it corresponds to, so the holder's own client can join that community's directory with the holder's address book — showing a star or a petname beside an entry — without either side telling the other. The community never learns the link exists; the contact never learns it either. A contact has at most one.

entryId.description: The entry, as that community's directory identifies it.

vtcDid.description: The DID of the community whose directory holds the entry.

DirectoryRef.title: DirectoryRef

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

ListId.description: Identifier of one of the holder's contact lists: a ULID in Crockford base32, uppercase, assigned by the agent when the list is created. Meaningful only inside the context that holds the list; it is never sent to anyone but the holder's own clients.
ListId.title: ListId

ListIds.description: The lists a contact is on, as a set: order carries no meaning. A contact on no list has no `lists` member, never an empty array, so there is one way to say "none".
ListIds.title: ListIds

Petname.description: The holder's private name for a contact, on one line: no control characters, line breaks included. A petname in Zooko's sense — chosen by the holder, meaningful to the holder, and unforgeable by anyone else, because nobody else can write it. Distinct from the contact's own disclosed `nickname` or display name, which the contact chose and may change. Compared exactly, as a string: an agent does not case-fold or normalise it.
Petname.title: Petname

Response.description: Success response to persona/contact/list. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/persona/contact/list/1.1#response. Summaries carry no claim values: a list is for finding a contact, and finding one does not require disclosing every contact's details. They do carry the holder's own annotations, which a client needs to sort, badge and filter, and which go to no one but the holder's own client.

displayName.description: A rendering hint drawn from the contact's own disclosed display-name claim, so a list is legible. Absent when they disclosed none; a producer MUST NOT substitute the DID — or the petname — silently as though it were the contact's own name.

hasUnreviewedChange.description: True when the current revision superseded another and the holder has not yet acknowledged the difference.

starred.description: Whether the holder starred the contact. Always present.

subjectDid.description: The DID the contact disclosed. Absent for a contact made from a community directory entry whose DID the holder has not been shown (persona/contact/put/1.1 and later, linking form).

Response.title: Persona Contact List — response payload

Ulid.description: A ULID in Crockford base32, uppercase. Used for `attributeId` and `profileId`. Chosen over a UUID because the leading 48 bits are a timestamp, so a key-ordered scan of the store is also creation-ordered and a `list` needs no secondary sort. Server-assigned on create; a producer MAY supply one to make a create idempotent, and a maintainer MUST reject a supplied value that already exists rather than silently overwriting.
Ulid.title: Ulid

schema.description: Enumerate contacts in a context, optionally narrowed to those known by one persona, those the holder starred, those on one of the holder's lists, or those linked to one community's directory. Summaries only, with the holder's annotations; documents are fetched one at a time. Filters combine as AND.

changedSince.description: Return only contacts whose current revision was received after this instant. Annotation changes do not count: they are the holder's own and need no "what changed while I was away".

directoryVtcDid.description: Only contacts whose `directoryRef` names this community. What the holder's own client asks for when it joins that community's directory with the holder's contacts, locally.

knownByPersona.description: Narrow to contacts known by this persona. Omitting it lists the context's contacts across every persona in it, which a producer SHOULD offer deliberately rather than by default — the unfiltered view is the one that shows the holder's personas side by side.

listId.description: Only contacts on this list. A list this context does not hold is `listUnknown`, not an empty page, because a list identifier is the holder's own and its absence is a definite answer worth giving.

starred.description: `true`: only starred contacts. `false`: only unstarred ones. Absent: both.

schema.title: Persona Contact List — payload
